newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELAN TAX EVASION CUT TO 50.5 PCT IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELAN TAX EVASION CUT TO 50.5 PCT IN 1997.

text.p: Venezuela's rate of tax evasion has dropped to 50.5 percent in 1997, compared with 60 percent in 1996, a top government official said Monday.

The reduction in tax evasion will bring tax revenues in 1997 to the equivalent of 9.6 percent of gross domestic product, National Taxation Superintendent Moraima Campos said during an event to mark the tax body SENIAT's third anniversary.
Tax evasion levels have been cut from over 70 percent since the creation of SENIAT by the introduction of stiffer penalties and easier payment facilities.

"SENIAT is an institution which represents the seed of modernization in the public sector; an institution which has overcome obstacles thrown in its path in these three years of operation," Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said at the event.
